scenes.script: CRISPR targeting. Everything depends on two RNAs and one permission signal.
The crRNA carries the address: a spacer copied from an old invader.
The tracrRNA is the handle Cas9 knows how to grab.
Together, they become the guide Cas9 can actually use.
Cas9 patrols DNA, but it does not read every base first.
It hunts for PAM, the short motif that says: check here.
No PAM, no cut. Even a perfect match gets ignored.
With PAM present, Cas9 pries open a few DNA bases.
The crRNA tests the exposed strand one base at a time.
A mismatch makes the complex let go.
A correct seed match makes the target worth testing fully.
A full match forms an R-loop inside the protein.
The HNH domain lines up with the strand matching the guide.
The RuvC domain lines up with the opposite strand.
The famous edit begins as a bacterial memory test.
Dual-RNA targeting is memory, scaffold, PAM, match, shape-change, cut.
